newsitem.title: USA: Worst U.S. spring flooding in a decade expected.
newsitem.headline: Worst U.S. spring flooding in a decade expected.

text.p: More of the country is expected to experience flooding this spring than in any year in the past decade, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said on Tuesday.

NOAA said prospects for severe flooding were high in the upper Midwest, and there were significant chances for some flooding in the West, and the Mississippi, lower Missouri and Ohio valleys, and in parts of the Southeast.
Substantial snow fell across north central and western sections of the country, leaving the potential for flooding from snow melt, NOAA said.

Heavy rainfall during February and early March caused devastating flooding in the Ohio valley, and some flooding continues across portions of the Southeast, the middle and lower Mississippi valley and the Great Lakes regions, it said.

NOAA hydrologists also said the Red River in North Dakota and Minnesota and the James River in South Dakota could see record flooding, and the northern and central Rocky Mountains could see severe flooding.

"We're very concerned that people recognize the dangers of floods and flash floods and take appropriate action," said Elbert Friday, Jr., NOAA assistant admnistrator for weather services. "During the recent flooding in the Ohio River basin more than 20 people lost their lives."
